copy.headline: Thanksgiving off to a chilly start in North Texas
copy.caption:
High temps will climb into the low- to mid-50s with abundant sunshine. Thanksgiving in North Texas is off to a cold start.

In fact, Thursday is one of the coldest mornings that North Texas has seen since March. A First Alert Weather Day is in effect this morning until 9 a.m. due to the first freeze of the season for many in North Texas, indicating the end of the growing season.

story.title: Thanksgiving off to a chilly start in North Texas
story.summary: High temps will climb into the low- to mid-50s with abundant sunshine. Updated on: November 26, 2026 / 7:23 AM CST / CBS Texas Thanksgiving in North Texas is off to a cold start. In fact, Thursday is one of the coldest mornings that North Texas has seen since March. A First Alert Weather Day is in effect this morning until 9 a.m. due to the first freeze of the season for many in North Texas, indicating the end of the growing season. If you're planning on running the Turkey Trot, dress warmly. Temperatures are dipping near or below 32 degrees across North Texas. Highs today will climb into the low to mid-50s with abundant sunshine. Winds will be from the north, gusting up to 20mph at times, which may make it feel even cooler out; grab a jacket.
